criteria.justification: The response explicitly invokes the senior stakeholder's point that 'a perfectly mapped system is useless if it doesn't solve the customer's actual math problem,' treating the paused-launch precedent as directly relevant rather than assuming mapping accuracy predicts customer value.

The engineering-facing metric is not kept primary; it is demoted to a diagnostic/regression gate while the customer-facing metric becomes the true measure of success, so the year of investment is not used to justify keeping the old metric as primary (though morale is cited as a reason to retain it operationally).

The response explicitly addresses the missing ground-truth data by proposing an Early Access/Closed Beta specifically designed to 'mine the missing ground-truth data' before GA, rather than treating the switch as immediately clean.

The response distinguishes 'health of our engine' vs 'success of our business' framing and structures gates around this, but it does not explicitly discuss how making the customer metric primary will redirect what the team optimizes for going forward beyond this one launch's scoring.
The response gives a concrete, phased recommendation—old metric as Beta release gate, new metric as GA gate—rather than merely listing tradeoffs.
